name: Harbour
desc: A container port at the bottom of the night — four ranks of ship-to-shore gantries stand off into sodium haze, each rank sliding at its own rate so the forest of legs opens and closes in parallax, trolleys crawl out along the booms and back, a boxed-up ship stands at the quay, and the whole lit mass lies broken on the water in bands that never stop sliding; sodium night, a cold Hopper dawn, pure silhouette planes, a cyan schematic, or thermal false-colour.

energy.doc: how hard the port burns — lamp brightness, sodium bloom through the haze, glow on the water and the sparkle in the chop

scale.doc: how big the steel stands — at max the near gantry is colossal and fills the frame, at min the whole port is a distant strip

density.doc: how crowded the port is — gantries per rank, boxes on the ship, number of lamps

speed.doc: parallax drift rate of the ranks and how fast the trolleys crawl the booms (0.15 still creeps)

haze.doc: atmosphere stacked between the ranks — aerial perspective, lamp bloom and the drifting veils

hue.doc: sodium hue — the whole light of the port keys off this

x.doc: lateral position of the port along the quay

y.doc: waterline as a canvas fraction — how much water lies in front of the port

style.doc: aesthetic: sodium-vapour night, the steel lost in orange light-pollution haze / a cold Hopper dawn, blue-grey silhouettes against a pale warm sky / pure flat silhouette planes stacked on a graded ground, no interior detail / a cyan setting-out schematic of the terminal / thermal false-colour, the lamps and the funnel the only hot things in a dead-cold port

seed.doc: layout lottery — gantry spacing, heights, box colours, lamp placement
